1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Philadelphia: Cost Guide

If you’re scrolling through Philadelphia’s endless list of junk‑removal services, chances are you’ve landed on 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? and wondered, “How much will this actually cost me?” You’re not alone. Pricing is the biggest driver of decision‑making for homeowners, renters, and business owners alike. In this guide we’ll walk through exactly how 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? determines its rates, what you can expect to pay for common clean‑outs, and smart ways to keep your bill low. By the end, you’ll have a clear picture of the price you’ll face and the confidence to book the right service for your Philadelphia junk‑removal needs.

Get a Free Quote from 1-800-GOT-JUNK? → Get a Free Quote from 1-800-GOT-JUNK?

How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Sets Its Prices

Volume‑Based Pricing, Not Item‑Based

Unlike many local haulers who charge by the pound or by the item, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? uses a volume‑based model. The team arrives in a large, color‑coded truck and fills it with the items you want removed. The more space you occupy, the higher the price. This approach eliminates guesswork about weight and ensures you only pay for the space you actually use.

Factors That Influence the Final Bill

  • Truck Size: 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? operates a fleet of 12‑ft, 16‑ft, and 20‑ft trucks. Larger trucks cost more, but they’re ideal for big estate clean‑outs.
  • Load Volume: The crew measures how much of the truck’s space your junk occupies. A half‑truck load costs roughly half the price of a full‑truck load.
  • Location: Philadelphia’s city limits, surrounding suburbs, and traffic patterns affect travel time and fuel costs.
  • Special Items: Items that require extra handling—like pianos, hot‑tub equipment, or hazardous waste—may incur additional fees.
  • Seasonality: Demand spikes in spring (spring‑cleaning) and fall (home‑renovation) can push prices up a few percent.

Typical Costs for Common Jobs in Philly

Below is a snapshot of what most Philadelphians pay when they call 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? for everyday junk removal. Prices are average estimates based on recent quotes in the Greater Philadelphia area. Your exact cost will vary depending on the factors above.

  • Single‑Room Clean‑Out (e.g., bedroom or office): $150‑$250. This usually fills about a quarter‑truck.
  • Kitchen Appliance Removal (fridge, stove, dishwasher): $180‑$300. Large appliances take up a lot of space, so the price leans toward a half‑truck load.
  • Yard Waste (branches, mulch, old patio stones): $120‑$200. Yard debris is compact, so you often get a lower rate per cubic foot.
  • Whole‑House Clean‑Out (post‑renovation or estate clean‑up): $500‑$1,200. Most full‑house jobs fill a 20‑ft truck, the highest tier.
  • Construction Debris (drywall, lumber, tiles): $250‑$600. If the debris is heavy, the crew might need a stronger truck, which adds a small surcharge.

Remember, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? offers a no‑hidden‑fees guarantee. The price you receive on the day of service is the price you pay—no surprise charges for labor, mileage, or disposal.

How to Get the Best Deal

Ask for a Free Quote

Before any truck rolls up, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? provides a free, no‑obligation estimate. The team will ask you a few quick questions about the type and amount of junk you have, then give you a price range. This step is your chance to compare against other local haulers and verify that the quoted cost aligns with your budget.

Get a Free Quote from 1-800-GOT-JUNK? → Book 1-800-GOT-JUNK Now

Combine Loads & Schedule Smartly

If you have multiple areas to clean—say a garage and a basement—consider scheduling them for the same day. The crew can load everything into one truck, saving you the cost of a second trip. Likewise, if you’re planning a major renovation, try to time the junk removal for the same week you finish the work. The less “dead‑head” mileage the driver makes, the more likely you’ll receive a volume discount.

Take Advantage of Seasonal Promotions

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? runs occasional discounts, especially in the off‑peak months of January and February. Sign up for their newsletter or follow them on social media to catch a coupon that could shave $20‑$50 off a full‑truck job.

FAQs About 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Pricing

Do I pay for disposal fees?

No. All disposal fees are baked into the quoted price. The company is licensed to dump the waste at approved facilities, so you never see a separate line item for landfill costs.

What if I have hazardous materials?

Items like paint cans, batteries, or chemicals require special handling. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? will identify these during the onsite assessment and provide a transparent surcharge—usually $50‑$100—so you won’t be blindsided.

Can I change the date after I’ve booked?

Yes. The service offers flexible scheduling with a 24‑hour notice window. If you need to reschedule, just call the local office and they’ll arrange a new time without penalty.
